passages.title: Green Energy Corridor Phase-III approved
passages.text:
The Union Cabinet approved the Green Energy Corridor Phase-III (GEC-III) scheme on 30 September 2026. The scheme has a total outlay of Rs 1,86,405 crore and aims to strengthen intra-state transmission so that up to 135 GW of renewable power can be evacuated by 2032-33.

Of this outlay, Rs 1,36,378 crore is for intra-state transmission infrastructure. A further Rs 50,000 crore is for battery energy storage, to deploy 50 GWh of Battery Energy Storage Systems.

The Centre will provide Central Financial Assistance (CFA) of Rs 54,082 crore. This support is intended to help offset intra-state transmission charges and so keep electricity costs lower for consumers.

State Transmission Utilities will be the overall implementing agencies. Greenfield transmission projects will be awarded through tariff-based competitive bidding (TBCB), while brownfield upgrades will follow a cost-plus basis. Transmission service providers will take part on a build-own-operate-maintain model.

statements: I. The National Green Hydrogen Mission was approved by the Union Cabinet on 4 January 2023.
II. The mission targets at least 10 million tonnes per annum of green hydrogen production capacity by 2030.
questions.explanation: Statement I is true. Statement II is false: the mission's target is at least 5 million metric tonnes per annum of green hydrogen production capacity by 2030.

questions.q: Electricity, as a subject, is placed at Entry 38 of the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution. Entry 38 belongs to which list?
questions.explanation: Entry 38 of List III (the Concurrent List) covers electricity, so both the Centre and the States can legislate on it. The Eighth and Eleventh Schedules are not lists of legislative subjects.

questions.q: In which year did India's non-fossil fuel sources come to account for 50 per cent of the country's total installed power capacity?
questions.explanation: The 50 per cent non-fossil share of installed capacity was reached in mid-2025 (June 2025 per The Statesman), five years ahead of the 2030 target.

questions.q: The Union Cabinet approved Phase II of the Green Energy Corridor in January 2022. What was the scheme's total estimated cost?
questions.explanation: Phase II was approved with a total estimated cost of about Rs 12,031.33 crore, with central financial assistance of 33 per cent of project cost.

list2: A. Constitution of a Finance Commission
B. Grants for any public purpose
C. Appointment of the Comptroller and Auditor-General by the President
D. Consolidated Fund and Public Account
questions.explanation: Article 266 creates the Consolidated Fund and Public Account; Article 280 provides for the Finance Commission; Article 282 allows grants for public purposes; Article 148 provides for the President's appointment of the CAG.

questions.assertion: The Green Energy Corridor Phase-III was enacted by Parliament as a statute in September 2026.
questions.reason: The Central Electricity Authority is constituted under Section 70 of the Electricity Act, 2003.
questions.explanation: A is false: GEC-III was approved by the Union Cabinet, not enacted as a law by Parliament. R is true: Section 70 of the Electricity Act, 2003 constitutes the CEA as a statutory body.

passages.title: T20 World Cup 2026: India's Super Eight run
passages.text:
The ICC Men's T20 World Cup 2026 was co-hosted by India and Sri Lanka. Pakistan had planned to boycott its match against India, but it dropped the boycott and agreed to play in Colombo. On 15 February, at the R. Premadasa Stadium, India beat Pakistan by 61 runs. Batting first, India scored 175 for seven in their 20 overs. Pakistan were bowled out for 114 in 18 overs. Ishan Kishan scored 77 off 40 balls. India, the defending champions, then moved on to the Super Eight stage.

The Super Eight stage had eight teams in two groups of four, and the top two in each group advanced to the semi-finals. India next beat Zimbabwe by 72 runs in Chennai on 26 February. On 1 March, in Kolkata, India beat West Indies by five wickets, with Sanju Samson unbeaten on 97 off 50 balls, a result that secured one of the four semi-final places. India were then set to meet England in the second semi-final at the Wankhede Stadium in Mumbai on 5 March.

list1: I. Captain of India when it won the inaugural 2007 ICC Men's T20 World Cup
II. Captain of India when it won the 2024 ICC Men's T20 World Cup
III. Captain of India in its match against Pakistan at Colombo in 2026
IV. Captain of Pakistan in its match against India at Colombo in 2026
questions.explanation: MS Dhoni captained India to the 2007 title, Rohit Sharma captained the 2024 title side, Suryakumar Yadav captained India against Pakistan in 2026 and Salman Ali Agha captained Pakistan in their match.

questions.assertion: The Dronacharya Award is conferred on sports coaches.
questions.reason: The Padma Shri is the fourth-highest civilian award of India.
questions.explanation: Both statements are true. The Dronacharya Award honours coaches; the Padma Shri's rank among civilian honours does not explain who receives the Dronacharya Award.

questions.q: In which city is the headquarters of the International Cricket Council (ICC) located?
questions.explanation: The ICC left Lord's and moved its headquarters to Dubai Sports City, Dubai, in 2005.

statements: I. India won the 2024 ICC Men's T20 World Cup final by seven runs.
II. India beat Pakistan by five runs in the final of the inaugural 2007 ICC Men's T20 World Cup.
questions.explanation: Both statements are true: India beat South Africa by seven runs in the 2024 final, and beat Pakistan by five runs in the 2007 final.

statements: 1. The Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna is India's highest sporting honour.
2. National Sports Day in India is observed on 29 August.
3. Major Dhyan Chand won Olympic hockey gold with India in 1928, 1932 and 1936.
4. The Padma Shri was instituted in 1954.
questions.explanation: All four statements are correct: the Khel Ratna is the highest sporting honour, National Sports Day falls on 29 August (Dhyan Chand's birthday), Dhyan Chand won Olympic hockey gold with India in 1928, 1932 and 1936, and the Padma Shri was instituted in 1954.

questions.q: The 2024 ICC Men's T20 World Cup final, which India won, was played in which country?
questions.explanation: The 2024 final was played at Kensington Oval in Barbados, where India beat South Africa.

passages.title: Chhattisgarh UCC panel
passages.text:
The Chhattisgarh cabinet, chaired by Chief Minister Vishnu Deo Sai, decided in April 2026 to set up a high-level committee to prepare a draft Uniform Civil Code for the state. Retired judge Ranjana Prakash Desai was named to lead the panel.

The General Administration Department issued the formal order on 25 June 2026, constituting a five-member panel. Its members include retired IAS officers Shatrughan Singh and M.K. Raut, senior advocate Mohan Pawar and retired principal Jyoti Rani Singh.

The committee is to study the feasibility of a Uniform Civil Code, review the personal laws governing marriage, divorce, maintenance, inheritance, succession and adoption, and recommend a legislative framework. It is to seek suggestions from citizens, social organisations and legal experts before finalising its recommendations.

The first meeting was scheduled for 24 July 2026. Chief Minister Sai has said the government will make every effort to table the Bill in the Assembly's winter session in December.

questions.assertion: Directive Principles of State Policy cannot be enforced by any court.
questions.reason: Directive Principles can be enforced through writ petitions filed in the High Courts.
questions.explanation: A is true: Article 37 states that the Directive Principles are not enforceable by any court. R is false: writ petitions are not the remedy for Directive Principles, which remain non-justiciable.

questions.q: Which Article guarantees freedom of conscience and the right to freely profess, practise and propagate religion, subject to public order, morality and health?
questions.explanation: Article 25(1) guarantees freedom of conscience and the right to profess, practise and propagate religion, subject to public order, morality, health and other Part III provisions. Article 16 concerns equality of opportunity in public employment, Article 29 concerns cultural and educational rights, and Article 300A concerns property.

questions.q: Chhattisgarh was formed in 2000 as India's 26th state after being carved out of which existing state?
questions.explanation: Chhattisgarh was formed on 1 November 2000 by partitioning southeastern districts of Madhya Pradesh under the Madhya Pradesh Reorganisation Act. Bihar, Odisha and Uttar Pradesh were not its parent state.

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution directs the State to endeavour to secure a Uniform Civil Code for citizens throughout India?
questions.explanation: Article 44, a Directive Principle in Part IV, directs the State to endeavour to secure a Uniform Civil Code throughout India. Article 19 lists certain freedoms, Article 300A protects property as a legal right, and Article 370 dealt with the special status of Jammu and Kashmir.

list2: B. Protection of environment and wildlife
C. Equal justice and free legal aid
questions.explanation: Article 39A provides for equal justice and free legal aid; Article 40 for organisation of village panchayats; Article 48A for protection of environment and wildlife; Article 51A lists the Fundamental Duties (Part IVA).

statements: I. Article 32 provides remedies for enforcement of the Fundamental Rights conferred by Part III.
II. Article 32 is placed in Part IV of the Constitution, which contains the Directive Principles of State Policy.
questions.explanation: Statement I is correct: Article 32 is the remedy for enforcing rights under Part III. Statement II is wrong because Article 32 sits in Part III, not Part IV. Answer: I only.

passages.title: Tiger re-introduction workshop, Alwar
passages.text:
Union minister Bhupender Yadav inaugurated a National Workshop on "Tiger Re-introduction: Opportunities & Challenges" in Alwar, Rajasthan, on 28 June 2026. The National Tiger Conservation Authority organised the event.

At the workshop, the Road Map on Active Management of Tigers in India was released. It provides a framework for managing tiger populations across reserves and landscapes, identifying potential source and sink areas and recommending ecological management strategies. A booklet on the reintroduction and recovery of tigers in India was released alongside it, together with the Project Cheetah annual report covering September 2024 to December 2025.

Yadav asked participants to identify potential source and sink populations and build science-based long-term management strategies. He stressed keeping ecological corridors open where tiger and elephant ranges overlap, and credited community participation for the successful tiger reintroductions at Panna and Sariska. He said tiger conservation goes beyond protecting a single species.

Citing national progress, Yadav said the number of tiger reserves had risen to 58 over the last decade.

questions.q: Jim Corbett National Park, the first national park brought under Project Tiger, is located in which Indian state?
questions.explanation: Jim Corbett National Park (part of Corbett Tiger Reserve) is in Uttarakhand; it was the first park brought under Project Tiger.

questions.q: The National Tiger Conservation Authority, a statutory body, functions under which ministry of the Government of India?
options: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
questions.explanation: NTCA is a statutory body under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, constituted under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 as amended in 2006.

questions.assertion: The Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve was India's first biosphere reserve.
questions.reason: The Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve lies entirely within the state of Kerala.
questions.explanation: A is true: Nilgiri was set up in 1986 as India's first biosphere reserve. R is false: the reserve spans Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Karnataka.

statements: I. Kuno National Park, where Project Cheetah was launched, lies in Rajasthan.
II. Gir National Park, the main home of the Asiatic lion, lies in Rajasthan.
questions.explanation: Neither is correct: Kuno National Park is in Madhya Pradesh and Gir National Park is in Gujarat.
Project Tiger was launched in 1973; Project Elephant in 1992; Project Cheetah was formally launched at Kuno on 17 September 2022; the Wildlife Institute of India was established at Dehradun in 1982.

questions.q: At the 2010 St Petersburg Tiger Summit, how many tiger-range governments committed to the TX2 goal of doubling wild tiger numbers?
questions.explanation: Thirteen tiger-range governments committed to TX2 at the 2010 St Petersburg Tiger Summit.

passages.title: Industry definition and labour codes
passages.text:
A nine-judge Constitution Bench has delivered its verdict on the meaning of "industry" in labour law, reconsidering the 1978 judgment in Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board v. A. Rajappa. That judgment had read the term widely, bringing within it establishments that are not manufacturing units.

The Supreme Court has held that the 1978 test continues to govern pending disputes under the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, which has since been repealed. For disputes arising under the Industrial Relations Code, 2020, however, the 1978 definition will not serve as the foundation for interpreting "industry"; the Code's definition must be read on its own text and context. The verdict was pronounced in August 2026.

list1: III. Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020
questions.explanation: The Code on Wages, 2019 repeals the Payment of Wages Act, 1936; the Code on Social Security, 2020 takes over the Employees' State Insurance Act, 1948; the OSH Code, 2020 replaces the Factories Act, 1948; and the Industrial Relations Code, 2020 subsumes the Trade Unions Act, 1926.

questions.q: From which date did the Industrial Relations Code, 2020 come into force?
questions.explanation: The Ministry of Labour and Employment notified 21 November 2025 as the date the Industrial Relations Code, 2020 came into force, together with the other labour codes.

questions.assertion: The Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act was enacted in 1966.
questions.reason: The Industrial Relations Code, 2020 subsumes the Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act, 1946.
questions.explanation: The assertion is false because the Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act is a 1946 enactment, as its name states. The reason is true: the Industrial Relations Code, 2020 subsumes three central Acts, including the Standing Orders Act, 1946.

statements: I. The Equal Remuneration Act, 1976 was repealed by the Code on Social Security, 2020.
II. The Payment of Bonus Act, 1965 was repealed by the Code on Wages, 2019.
questions.explanation: Section 69(1) of the Code on Wages, 2019 repeals the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, the Minimum Wages Act, 1948, the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965 and the Equal Remuneration Act, 1976. So statement II is correct and statement I wrongly names the Code on Social Security as the repealing Code.

questions.q: Begar, which is unpaid compulsory labour, is prohibited under which Article of the Constitution of India?
questions.explanation: Article 23 prohibits traffic in human beings, begar and other similar forms of forced labour, and makes any contravention an offence punishable under law.

statements: 1. The right against exploitation is a fundamental right under Part III of the Constitution.
2. The 1978 Bangalore Water Supply judgment on the meaning of "industry" was delivered by a seven-judge Bench.
3. The nine-judge Bench that heard the 2026 reference on the "industry" definition was headed by Justice B.V. Nagarathna.
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong because the nine-judge Bench was headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, with Justice Nagarathna as a member. Two statements are correct, so the answer is Only two.
